status.nb: 31 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Damaskus, Quneitra og Aleppo.

summary.en: Syrian authorities abducted a suspect in an Assad-era massacre from Lebanon and arrested the “Butcher of Baniyas” for the 2013 coastal massacres, while two Syrian pipelines were damaged in recent attacks on energy infrastructure. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu spoke directly with President Ahmed al-Sharaa after a 2025 strike in Damascus, a conversation that Syrian sources said involved U.S. and Arab mediation, and a Druze leader praised Netanyahu’s intervention. A Syrian soldier was killed and another seriously injured while clearing mines in the Homs countryside. Authorities foiled an ISIS plot to target a police patrol in Damascus countryside. The conflict produced 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Syriske myndigheter bortførte en mistenkt i et massakre under Assad-æra fra Libanon og arresterte «Baniyas-slakteren» for kystmassakrene i 2013, mens to syriske rørledninger ble skadet i nylige angrep på energiinfrastruktur. Israels statsminister Netanyahu snakket direkte med president Ahmed al-Sharaa etter et angrep i Damaskus i 2025, en samtale som syriske kilder sa involverte amerikansk og arabisk mekling, og en drusisk leder roste Netanyahus inngripen. En syrisk soldat ble drept og en annen ble alvorlig såret mens de ryddet miner på landsbygda i Homs. Myndighetene avverget et IS-plan om å angripe en politipatrulje på landsbygda i Damaskus. Konflikten førte til 2 732 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
background.extract: Disputes and clashes in Syria have continued following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, which many sources consider the end of the Syrian civil war. Numerous actors are involved, including clashes between the newly-formed Syrian caretaker government and later the Syrian transitional government led by the former emir of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) and incumbent president Ahmed al-Sharaa, Assad loyalists, Alawite groups, and Druze insurgents; clashes between elements of the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army (SNA) and the government on one side, and formerly the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on the other; as well as an Israeli invasion and occupation of the demilitarized buffer zone in southwestern Syria.
